=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:lines 112-116 (import block), lines 629-632 (_load_quarantine_runtime), lines 664-718 (_persist_quarantine_runtime) | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Removing the quarantine helpers makes the verifier's quarantine import fail open, so the quarantine index is always empty and no `FINGERPRINT_QUARANTINED_V1` markers are emitted or persisted.
  WHY: Every reviewer traced the runtime path to a silent no-op, breaking the Phase 4A quarantine model that the audit depends on.
- scripts/drift_audit.sh:_recheck_cluster (lines ~495-530; early return at `if "FINGERPRINT_QUARANTINED_V1" not in cluster["marker_types"]: return {"applicable": False, ...}`) | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `_recheck_cluster` skips any cluster that lacks `FINGERPRINT_QUARANTINED_V1`, so PRE_EXISTING-only clusters are never rechecked against merged PR diffs.
  WHY: This blocks automatic closure of resolved pre-existing drift and leaves tracker issues open until manual intervention or timeout.
- scripts/drift_audit.sh:_parse_pre_existing_marker (line ~133: `if "PRE_EXISTING_FINGERPRINT_DRIFT_V1" not in line or " unchanged " not in line`) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The pre-existing marker parser only accepts markers containing `" unchanged "`, so `fixed_by_resolver` observations are silently dropped.
  WHY: The audit loses signal for drift that was temporarily fixed and can miss re-emergence until a new `unchanged` marker appears.
- scripts/drift_audit.sh:_parse_pre_existing_marker (line ~148: `if path is None: return None`) | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The parser returns `None` when `path` is missing, so any log-format change that omits or alters the field drops the marker.
  WHY: This tightly couples the audit to a specific marker layout and makes it fragile to small format changes.
- scripts/drift_audit.sh:_decode_json_at / _consume_json_string | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Marker JSON decoding lacks bounds/robustness checks, so truncated or malformed log lines can throw during parsing.
  WHY: A single bad log line can crash the audit instead of skipping the malformed marker.
- scripts/drift_audit.sh:_normalize_fp_key / _build_clusters | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `_normalize_fp_key` can return `None`, and callers do not guard before downstream dict lookups.
  WHY: Malformed markers can turn into runtime exceptions instead of being rejected cleanly.
- scripts/drift_audit.sh:_fetch_latest_merged_linked_prs / _fetch_pr_files / _recheck_cluster | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: GraphQL and PR-file fetch failures are fail-open, so a transient API/rate-limit error leaves the tracker open without a retry or distinct sentinel.
  WHY: One flaky request can keep a resolved drift cluster open for another audit cycle or longer.
- .github/workflows/drift-audit.yml + scripts/drift_audit.sh:_gh_ok / _gh_json | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Falling back to `GITHUB_TOKEN` and continuing on GH command failures can leave issue create/edit/close operations silently under-scoped or incomplete.
  WHY: In repos where `GITHUB_TOKEN` lacks issue permissions, the audit can fail open and leave stale tracker issues behind.
- scripts/drift_audit.sh:main() / _tracker_issue_lookup | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The lookup-update-create path for tracker issues has no lock or compare-and-swap protection.
  WHY: Concurrent runs can duplicate tracker issues or lose updates when two jobs act on the same cluster at once.
- scripts/drift_audit.sh:_fetch_latest_merged_linked_prs (around line 380) | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: Issue numbers are interpolated directly into the GraphQL query string without escaping.
  WHY: If the metadata shape changes unexpectedly, the batch query can break with invalid GraphQL syntax.
- scripts/drift_audit.sh:_fetch_pr_files | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The PR-files cache/dictionary path has no atomicity or fencing for concurrent runs.
  WHY: Overlapping workflow dispatches can race on the same data and produce inconsistent fetch results.
- scripts/drift_audit.sh:_fetch_run_log / _list_recent_runs | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The audit downloads and holds full logs for up to 200 runs per invocation with no tail/stream limit.
  WHY: Busy repos can waste significant API quota and memory, and large logs can slow or OOM the runner.
- scripts/drift_audit.sh:_recheck_cluster / _fetch_latest_merged_linked_prs / _fetch_pr_files (transient failure handling) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Transient GraphQL or PR-file failures are treated as inconclusive and keep the tracker open, with no retry/backoff or distinct retry sentinel.
  WHY: A single rate-limit event or network blip can leave a resolved cluster open for another audit cycle.
- scripts/label_helpers.sh:lines 44-49 (removal from `_AI_LABEL_COLORS`) and lines 83-88 (removal from `_AI_LABEL_DESCS`) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Removing `ai:resolver-escalated` from the label color/description maps makes `ensure_label_exists` fall back to generic blue text and a generic description.
  WHY: The label still exists, but the escalation signal is less visible in GitHub UI and diverges from existing tests/operational expectations.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:lines 112-116 (import block), lines 629-632 (_load_quarantine_runtime), lines 664-718 (_persist_quarantine_runtime) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The PR removes `_load_quarantine_list` and `_persist_quarantine_list` from `scripts/ai_memory.py` and removes the quarantine helpers from `scripts/ai_memory_lib.py`, but `scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py` still imports them through a fail-open `try/except`.
  WHY: `_load_quarantine_runtime()` returns the default empty payload without reading persisted state, `_persist_quarantine_runtime()` returns immediately, and no `FINGERPRINT_QUARANTINED_V1` markers can ever be produced.
- scripts/drift_audit.sh (Python heredoc): _recheck_cluster function (lines ~495-530 in the PR diff), the early-return at `if "FINGERPRINT_QUARANTINED_V1" not in cluster["marker_types"]: return {"applicable": False, ...}` | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `_recheck_cluster` short-circuits on clusters that do not contain `FINGERPRINT_QUARANTINED_V1`.
  WHY: Clusters formed solely from `PRE_EXISTING_FINGERPRINT_DRIFT_V1` markers are never rechecked against the merged PR diff, so they cannot auto-close.
- scripts/drift_audit.sh (Python heredoc): _parse_pre_existing_marker — the guard `" unchanged " not in line` | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The parser only accepts the literal substring `" unchanged "` and silently drops `fixed_by_resolver` markers.
  WHY: The audit misses a class of PRE_EXISTING observations and can be blind to re-emergence after a temporary fix.
- scripts/drift_audit.sh (Python heredoc): _fetch_latest_merged_linked_prs (GraphQL batch) and _fetch_pr_files (pagination loop), consumed by _recheck_cluster | severity=medium | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Transient API failures in GraphQL batch queries or PR file fetches are treated as fail-open.
  WHY: A failed GraphQL response yields an empty mapping and a failed PR-files fetch keeps the tracker open without any retry or sentinel.
- scripts/drift_audit.sh (Python heredoc): _fetch_run_log — calls `gh run view <id> --log` with no output limit | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The full workflow log is fetched into memory as a single string.
  WHY: Large review_autofix logs can consume substantial runner memory.
- scripts/drift_audit.sh (Python heredoc): _list_recent_runs fetches up to 100 runs per workflow × 2 workflows = up to 200 run metadata entries; _fetch_run_log then fetches the full log for each run | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The script fetches every log in the 24h window even when the runs have zero drift markers.
  WHY: This wastes GitHub API rate limit budget and runner time on busy repos.
- scripts/label_helpers.sh:lines 44-49 (removal from `_AI_LABEL_COLORS`) and lines 83-88 (removal from `_AI_LABEL_DESCS`) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `ai:resolver-escalated` label entry was removed from both associative arrays.
  WHY: `ensure_label_exists` falls back to a generic blue color and generic description, so the label loses its distinctive red color and escalation text in the GitHub UI.
